candidate_title: Step-Audio: Unified Understanding and Generation in Intelligent Speech Interaction

review_output.decision_rationale: Stage 2 evaluation finds explicit evidence of preference-learning components in the Step-Audio paper: (i) RLHF usage with a Reward Model and PPO training, including preference data construction (TQTA/AQTA) and a Bradley-Terry loss, which fulfills the defined preference-learning criteria; (ii) application within the audio domain (Step-Audio focuses on real-time speech interaction and audio-enabled capabilities) and (iii) the work is an original research article with concrete contributions (architecture, data engine, instruction-driven control, tool use) rather than a survey. These points satisfy all Stage 2 inclusion criteria and exclude the listed exclusions (no survey, explicit learning components present, not solely evaluative).

candidate_title: A differentiable perceptual audio metric learned from just noticeable differences

review_output.decision_rationale: Stage 2 canonical eligibility satisfied: the paper reports a learning framework for audio preference via pairwise judgments (are two recordings identical or not) to train a differentiable perceptual audio metric. It uses AB-style comparisons between two audio signals (reference xref and perturbed xper) and is applied within the audio domain; it is original research (not a survey). The full text provides explicit descriptions of AB-style judgments and data collection via crowdsourcing, aligning with the Stage 2 criteria. No retrieval or metadata ambiguities that would imply semantic_non_fit; no evidence of source_gold_tension.
